content.text: {"primary_meaning":"The pearl most commonly symbolizes the incomparable worth of the kingdom of God—and, by extension, salvation or life in Christ—worth surrendering everything else to obtain.","primary_basis":["Matthew 13:45–46 — the merchant and the pearl of great price is the principal basis; the parable presents the kingdom of heaven as supremely valuable.","Matthew 7:6 — “pearls” represent something sacred and precious, often understood as divine truth or the gospel, reinforcing the general symbolism of spiritual value.","Revelation 21:21 — the pearl gates of the New Jerusalem associate pearls with the beauty, glory, and immeasurable value of the final redeemed order."],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"Christ himself is the pearl of great price, whom the believer seeks and values above everything else.","basis":["Matthew 13:45–46","Philippians 3:8 is often used as a thematic parallel, though it does not mention pearls."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"The pearl represents the Church or redeemed people, while the merchant represents Christ, who gives all to acquire them.","basis":["Matthew 13:45–46","Ephesians 5:25 is sometimes cited as a thematic parallel concerning Christ giving himself for the Church."],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Pearls symbolize sacred teaching, gospel truth, or wisdom that should not be offered to those who will contemptuously profane it.","basis":["Matthew 7:6","Job 28:18 in translations that compare wisdom with pearls."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Pearls symbolize the splendor, purity, or preciousness of the New Jerusalem and entrance into the consummated kingdom.","basis":["Revelation 21:21"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Pearls signify extravagant wealth, luxury, or ostentatious adornment, sometimes with a negative connotation.","basis":["1 Timothy 2:9","Revelation 17:4","Revelation 18:12,16"],"prominence":"common"}],"has_settled_consensus":false,"confidence":"high","notes":"There is a strong dominant association between pearls and exceptional spiritual preciousness, especially the supreme value of the kingdom in Matthew 13:45–46. However, there is no fully settled one-to-one symbolic referent across Scripture: context can make the pearl represent the kingdom, Christ, sacred truth, redeemed glory, or material luxury. Even within the pearl-of-great-price parable, interpreters differ over whether the pearl specifically represents the kingdom or Christ, and whether the merchant represents the seeker or Christ."}
